1.why: access() resolves the account solely from the server-side session's userId and noId() rejects any body containing userId/accountId/emailOwner, so only the session owner's MFA data can be touched.

2.why: Verification codes derive from a per-account encrypted secret with a used flag, so a code from one account cannot verify another (and only the single demo account exists).

3.why: Nothing in /api/mfa/verify invalidates or rotates sessions, so any pre-existing sessions (other than the cookie replaced at sign-in) continue to work after MFA is enabled.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-GCM encrypted (encrypt()) and recovery codes are stored only as salted PBKDF2-SHA-256 hashes (210k iterations).

5.why: All secrets, session tokens, CSRF tokens, base32 seeds and recovery codes come from crypto.getRandomValues, a CSPRNG.

6.why: The only cookie is mfa_session with HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict, and the client keeps secrets/CSRF in JS variables with no localStorage/sessionStorage use.

7.why: Server-side validators email(), phone(), otp() and recovery() plus body-size and JSON-shape checks validate all input; data lives in Maps so no SQL injection surface exists.

8.why: The client renders all dynamic values via textContent (never innerHTML) and a nonce-based CSP blocks injected script execution.

9.why: The application issues no redirects at all and noId() explicitly rejects any 'redirect' field, so no open redirect is possible, though no formal allow-list exists.

10.why: headers() sets CSP with nonces and frame-ancestors 'none', HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy and Cache-Control on every response.

11.why: Set-Cookie for mfa_session includes HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict with a Max-Age, both at issuance and clearing on logout.

12.why: The client deliberately writes the mock OTP and all recovery codes into the on-page logs panel and console (log("Mock MFA OTP delivered: "...), log("Recovery codes delivered: "...)), and the seed sits in the otpauth URL query string, though server errors are generic with no stack traces.

13.why: TOTP codes are 30-second time-bound with a 10-minute provisioning window and the used flag blocks reuse after verification, and recovery codes are single-use (spliced on success), though recovery codes never expire and a TOTP can be retried within its window before first success.

14.why: wrong()/locked() lock OTP and recovery verification for 5 minutes after 5 failures, and reissue is capped at 3 per 10 minutes with 429 responses.

15.why: Sign-in deletes the old session and issues a fresh random identifier, sessions enforce 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and /api/logout deletes the session and expires the cookie.
